subject: ventures/uk-payments-on-account-calculator
professional: a UK chartered tax adviser (CTA) who prepares Self Assessment returns for sole traders, landlords and employees with side income; first checks: is the relevant amount income tax plus Class 4 less tax at source (TMA 1970 s59A(1)), are the GBP 1,000 and 20%/80% exemptions applied with the right boundary, are the 31 January / 31 July dates and the balancing payment right, is everything that is income tax (including the High Income Child Benefit Charge) inside the payment-on-account base and CGT/student loan/Class 2 outside it, and is an SA303 reduction measured on the same net-of-source basis as the original instalments (s59A(4))

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against sources the author did not write: gov.uk 'Understanding your Self Assessment tax bill: payments on account' (https://www.gov.uk/understand-self-assessment-bill/payments-on-account, fetched 2026-11-19 through the proxy, 200) and TMA 1970 s59A (legislation.gov.uk, fetched, 200), ITEPA 2003 s681B (fetched, 200). PASS: gov.uk worked example with no previous payments on account (bill GBP 3,000 -> January 4,500, July 1,500) reproduces exactly; gov.uk example with POAs already made (3,000 bill, 1,800 paid -> balancing 1,200, January 2,700, July 1,500) reproduces; s59A(1)(c) GBP 1,000 boundary (999.99 none, 1,000 due, 'not less than'); s59A(1)(d) 20% proportion boundary (8,000 of 10,000 at source still due, 8,000.01 exempt) matches gov.uk 'more than 80%'; s59A(2) dates 31 Jan 2027 / 31 Jul 2027 for 2026/27; overpayment netting (4,000 bill, 5,000 paid -> January 1,000). FAIL 1: the High Income Child Benefit Charge is 'a charge to income tax' (ITEPA 2003 s681B(1)), so it is part of the assessed amount in s59A(1)(a), and gov.uk's exclusion list names only capital gains and student loans; the tool tells users to put HICBC in 'other amounts' (index.html:72) and says it is not part of the relevant amount (calc.mjs:91): IT+C4 6,000 plus HICBC 2,000 gives instalments of 3,000 instead of 4,000, January 11,000 instead of 12,000, July 3,000 instead of 4,000. FAIL 2: s59A(4) reduces each instalment to 50% of the stated amount by which the expected assessment 'will exceed the amount of income tax deducted at source'; the tool asks for gross expected income tax + Class 4 (index.html:73, calc.mjs:31) and halves it against a net instalment (calc.mjs:75). With 10,000 tax and 5,000 PAYE (instalments 2,500) and a gross expectation of 6,000 (5,000 still through PAYE, net 1,000), the correct reduced instalment is 500; the tool says 'Your expected 2026/27 bill (GBP 6,000) is not below last year's, so a reduction claim would not help', which is wrong twice (6,000 is below 10,000, and the claim would cut 4,000 of payments). Core arithmetic right, two rule errors on common cases: 2.
evidence.completeness: Every feature the README and page list works end to end in Chromium (Playwright, served over http://127.0.0.1): balancing payment, both instalments, 31 January cash total, GBP 1,000 and 80% exemptions, reduction finding, dated payment schedule table, monthly set-aside in the text summary, checklist table, example button, clear, download-as-text and print buttons, usage opt-out; no console errors; no horizontal scroll at 360 px (scrollWidth 360). The reduction feature works only for users with nothing deducted at source (see correctness). Live page https://marisstella.app/uk-payments-on-account-calculator/ returns 200 and its llms.txt carries the marisstella.app URL. No TODOs or stubs. 3.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject dir: 26 tests, 26 pass, 94 ms; the README's root-relative command gives the same. Tests pin the sample, both threshold boundaries, netting, other amounts, the reduction maths for a no-PAYE case, dates and input rejection. Six mutants with quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (1,000 boundary < -> <=, firstTime always true, July year), 3 SURVIVED: sourceShare denominator including 'other' (calc.mjs:46), balancing-payment finding shown at zero (calc.mjs:67), and nextLabel set to the return year so every instalment is labelled 2025/26 instead of 2026/27 (calc.mjs:42). No test exercises a PAYE user's reduction, HICBC, or the page script's run() (page.test.mjs only greps the HTML). 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (104 lines), index.html (182), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs. Pure functions, bad input rejected rather than clamped, HTML escaped before innerHTML, storage guarded. Defects: the money formatter is written twice, as money() in calc.mjs:14 and gbp() in index.html:139; a net overpayment with no instalments shows the headline 'Due 2027-01-31: -£700' (index.html:156) instead of 'refund/credit'; '1,200' passed to compute() gives the misleading message 'Enter ... as zero or more' (calc.mjs:23; in Chromium the number input strips the comma so the page itself computes 1,200 correctly); nextLabel fallback string built but never reached for listed years. Small and reviewable: 3.
evidence.claims: Checked 9 claims. Backed: '31 January and 31 July' (calc.mjs:43-44, s59A(2)); 'each half of last year's relevant bill' (calc.mjs:54); GBP 1,000 and 80% exemptions (calc.mjs:51-52, gov.uk); 'about 150%' first year (gov.uk 4,500 on a 3,000 bill); monthly set-aside, schedule, checklist (all render); 'nothing uploaded' (page.test.mjs greps for fetch/XHR, usage.mjs is local storage only); disclaimer and 'written from memory' disclosure in README, VENTURE.yaml, page header and footer; llms.txt served with the live URL. Not backed: 'the High Income Child Benefit Charge ... not part of the relevant amount' (calc.mjs:91, repeated in the 'other amounts' label index.html:72) contradicts ITEPA s681B and gov.uk; 'see ... what a reduction claim would defer' is wrong for anyone with tax at source, and the finding text 'not below last year's' (calc.mjs:81) can be false on its face. Two unbacked claims a user would act on: 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job for three users. A sole trader with no PAYE and no child benefit: gets the right January and July figures and a correct reduction estimate (sample 6,400 -> 9,600 and 3,200; estimate 4,000 -> instalments 2,000). An employee with rental or freelance income taxed partly through PAYE (the main reason the 'deducted at source' field exists) who expects lower side income: told a reduction would not help when it would cut the instalments by 4,000 in the test case. A parent paying HICBC through Self Assessment (a large, common group): instalments understated by half the charge each, so the July bill arrives higher than the tool said. Also not modelled: coding a balancing payment under GBP 3,000 into the next year's PAYE code, which changes the 31 January cash figure for many employees, and a 2024/25 option for late filers. 2.
evidence.domain: Against TMA 1970 s59A and gov.uk: the relevant-amount definition, both exemption tests with their boundaries, the dates, balancing payment, CGT/student loan/Class 2 exclusion, interest on an over-reduced claim and the SA303 route all match. A CTA would stop at two points first: HICBC is income tax and belongs in the instalment base (s681B), and a reduction claim states the expected excess over tax deducted at source (s59A(4)), so the input must be net of PAYE. Both depart from the statute on common fact patterns: 2.

defects.what: The High Income Child Benefit Charge is a charge to income tax (ITEPA 2003 s681B) and so part of the payment-on-account base under TMA 1970 s59A(1); the tool tells users to enter it under 'other amounts' and states it is not part of the relevant amount, understating each instalment by half the charge (IT+C4 6,000 plus HICBC 2,000: instalments 3,000 instead of 4,000, July bill 1,000 short)

Reduction claim compares half the GROSS expected income tax + Class 4 with a NET-of-source instalment; s59A(4) uses the expected excess over tax deducted at source. A PAYE user (10,000 tax, 5,000 at source, expects 6,000 gross with 5,000 still at source) is told 'not below last year's, a reduction claim would not help' when the instalments could fall from 2,500 to 500

Same root: the 'other amounts' and estimate labels steer the input wrongly ('CGT, student loan, child benefit charge'; 'Expected income tax + Class 4 NIC next year' with no 'after tax deducted at source')

3 of 6 seeded mutants survive: nextLabel mislabelling every instalment year, the 80% test denominator, and the balancing finding at zero; no test covers a PAYE reduction, HICBC, or the page script's run()
Coding a balancing payment under GBP 3,000 into the next PAYE code (which changes the 31 January cash figure for many employees) is not mentioned, and there is no 2024/25 option for late filers
A net overpayment with no instalments shows the headline 'Due 2027-01-31: -£700' instead of a refund/credit wording
Money formatter duplicated (money() in calc.mjs, gbp() in the page); '1,200' passed to compute() gives the misleading 'as zero or more' error (the page's number input strips the comma in Chromium)

verdict: A small, honest, well-disclaimed payments-on-account calculator whose core arithmetic matches both gov.uk worked examples exactly (3,000 bill: 4,500 then 1,500; with 1,800 paid: 2,700 then 1,500) and whose GBP 1,000 and 80% exemption boundaries and dates match TMA 1970 s59A. Two rule errors hit common users: it excludes the High Income Child Benefit Charge from the instalment base although ITEPA s681B makes it income tax, so instalments are understated by half the charge, and it measures an SA303 reduction on gross rather than net-of-PAYE expected tax, telling an employee with side income that a reduction 'would not help' when s59A(4) would cut each instalment from 2,500 to 500. Tests pass (26) but 3 of 6 seeded mutants survive. Everything it lists works, so it is finished, but correctness, claims and verification are 2, so it does not meet the bar.
